title: Raw and derived upper-truncation comparisons
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories with derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume C has enough injectives and K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let F:C\to D be additive and preserve finite limits [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For any integer-indexed cochain complex I [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and n\in\mathbf Z, write a:\tau_{\le n}I\to I for the canonical upper smart truncation inclusion [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Both H^n(F(a)) and H^n(RF(Q(a))) are isomorphisms. Here F(a) is termwise application, Q is localization, and RF is the total right derived functor. No K-injectivity of I is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05TC (2), lemma-negative-vanishing; raw kernel calculation in Tag 0AVW

proof.text: Finite-limit preservation gives a canonical isomorphism from F of cycles to cycles of the mapped short complex. Its naturality follows by cancellation of the cycle inclusion. For the upper-truncation inclusion, the degree n-1 component is invertible, the degree n component is monic, and the homology map is invertible. Apply the epi diagram lemma to cycles -> homology and use monicity to prove its cycle map invertible. Transport through the kernel comparison and use isIso_homologyMap_of_isIso_cyclesMap_of_epi to obtain the raw comparison.

The quotient of the upper-truncation inclusion is quasi-isomorphic to tau>=n+1 I. Take the distinguished triangle of the truncation short exact sequence and apply RF. Lift tau>=n+1 I to the bounded-below category, use negative vanishing there, and transport along bounded-below/unbounded compatibility and the quotient quasi-isomorphism. Derived homology of the third term is zero in degrees n-1 and n, so isIso_homologyMap_mor1 gives the derived comparison.

    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (I.ιTruncLE n)) n) ∧

      (F.rightDerivedFunctor.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map (I.ιTruncLE n))))
